faculty_comment: Core conceptual hierarchy: Operating systems are the premier archetype of system software.
Direct architectural dependency: Distributed operating systems require computer network routing to share resources.
Foundational distributed design pattern: Network applications run as client-server processes over OS sockets.
Decentralized architecture: P2P overlay networks operate across interconnected computer network nodes.
Direct, essential connection: Unix/POSIX treats network sockets as file descriptors; core syllabus crossover.
State coordination and three-way synchronization share foundational concurrency mechanisms.
Hardware networking cards use DMA engines to move packet frames into host memory without CPU intervention.
Both represent textbook abstraction paradigms decoupling logical addressing spaces from underlying physical resources.
Network sockets are the distributed extension of Unix IPC mechanisms like pipes and message queues.
